questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the 7 common strong acids?
questions.explain: Hydrofluoric acid ($HF$) is a weak acid. $HCl$, $HNO_3$, and $H_2SO_4$ are strong acids.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Strong and Weak Acids and Bases

questions.q: What distinguishes a strong acid from a weak acid?
options: A strong acid is always more concentrated than a weak acid.
A strong acid dissociates completely in water, while a weak acid dissociates partially.
A strong acid has a higher pH than a weak acid.
A strong acid cannot be neutralized by a base.
questions.explain: The strength of an acid refers to its ability to ionize or dissociate. Strong acids dissociate 100%, whereas weak acids exist in equilibrium with their ions.

questions.q: Select the strong base from the list below.
questions.explain: Barium hydroxide ($Ba(OH)_2$) is a Group 2 metal hydroxide and is considered a strong base. Ammonia and methylamine are weak bases; aluminum hydroxide is insoluble/weak.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Strong and Weak Acids and Bases

questions.q: Which acid is considered strong because it fully ionizes in solution?
questions.explain: Perchloric acid ($HClO_4$) is one of the standard strong acids.
